author: Brittny Mejia

Philippine authorities on Thursday named Markle Jr. as a person of interest in their investigation into more than 7,000 images and a video — all of underage girls and boys — recovered from digital devices allegedly belonging to Markle Sr. At a press conference in Manila, the country’s Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla described the images as “deplorable” and “deeply, deeply disturbing.”

He was asked to leave a rehab center in Florida following news of the probe in the Philippines and moved to a nursing home, according to a report published by The Sun. In a previous statement to the Times, Meghan said she was “deeply distressed” by the news. The Duchess of Sussex said she first learned of “troubling and disturbing allegations” against her father in 2018, after a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection and later shared with her.

“Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children,” she said. Meghan’s relationship with her father has been the focus of intense media scrutiny since 2018, when she and Prince Harry tied the knot. Thomas Markle Sr.

did not attend the wedding. “I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them.”
